post.summary: Set a PIN
post.description: Owners and managers for anyone; everyone for themselves. Clears a lockout. Not idempotency-keyed on purpose: the request would be stored with the PIN in it, and setting the same PIN twice is harmless. Not with an API key: a person signs in for this.

post.summary: Switch to a staff member with their PIN
post.description: Any member of the company. On a paired counter device the person is then switched in: everything done there is theirs, with their access, until someone else switches in or the device locks. On a person's own sign-in the answer opens an `operator_session`: send its id as the X-Operator-Session header and core acts as the person switched in, with their access and their name on what they do, for up to 12 hours; the signed-in person's own PIN ends it (switching back). Access is the same rule as the panel's: a person's own sign-in decides when they have one, their title (Manager, Technician, Front desk) when they only have a PIN. After 5 wrong PINs in a row the PIN is locked for 15 minutes. Failed attempts are counted even though the request fails. Not with an API key: a person signs in for this.

post.summary: Complete a sale on a register
post.description: Any member, on a register with an open shift. A product line sold at another price than the store's catalog price needs an owner or a manager; the catalog price is kept with it. So do discounts over 10% (Settings → Users and roles): a line's own discount over 10% of the line, its share of a sale discount (`sale_discount_minor`) over 10% of it, or all the discounts over 10% of the items (gift cards are not counted); someone switched in with their PIN gives them as themselves. Totals and tax are worked out here from the lines; the payments must add up to what is due (the total less deposits already taken on the repairs it pays). Products leave stock (never below what open repairs hold), repairs are collected, store credit is used, and the sale gets the register's next receipt number. A card payment with `card_payment_id` must be approved, in this store, for the same amount, and not on another sale. A line with `gift_card` sells a gift card (no tax) and loads it; a `gift` payment takes from the card's balance, never below zero. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key after a lost answer: the sale is never recorded twice.

post.summary: Refund part or all of a sale
post.description: Owners and managers. Each line gives back its share of what was paid for it (the last units exactly what is left). Products can go back on the shelf with a `return` movement at their cost. Cash comes out of the drawer of an open shift on the given register; store credit goes to the sale's customer. Card goes back to the cards the sale was paid with on the store's reader (Stripe, sent in the background: see `card_refunds`), never more than they paid; a sale paid on a separate terminal is refunded there and recorded here. A defective unit can be `set_aside` instead of going back on the shelf: it becomes a defective unit of the store (`defective` on the product), to go back to the supplier on a supplier return. A sale is refunded once every unit is.
